summary: Correct, minimal fix for block-end markers (<|end_message|>/<|content_model_end_sampling|>) leaking into content when a combined reasoning+tool parser handles plain text with no tool call. The engine now distinguishes a block-end that closes a forwarded tool call (kept as content for the second pass) from one that ends ordinary content/reasoning (consumed via the normal transition). Well covered by new streaming and non-streaming tests parametrized over both terminals; the full parser-engine suite (3741 tests) stays green.
actions_taken: Read the diff and the surrounding code: vllm/parser/engine/streaming_parser_engine.py (_on_terminal skip-tool-parsing branch, new _tool_end_terminals set and _tool_call_passthrough_open flag), vllm/parser/abstract_parser.py (_extract_tool_calls no-tool-calls branch), vllm/parser/inkling.py (transition table: block-end terminals THINK_END/END_SAMPLING carry TOOL_CALL_END only from TOOL_ARGS), and tests/parser/engine/test_inkling.py + conftest.

Traced the skip-tool-parsing (reasoning) pass: a block-end after a forwarded tool call (passthrough open) is emitted as content so the second tool pass can re-parse the complete tool block; a block-end for content/reasoning (no passthrough) routes through the normal transition, so it is dropped or fires REASONING_END. Confirmed this matches the existing round-trip test (test_skip_tool_parsing_round_trip) which still expects 2 tool blocks preserved in content and reasoning=='plan'.

Ran pytest tests/parser/engine/test_inkling.py -q -> 55 passed. Ran pytest tests/parser/engine/ -q -> 3741 passed (the change is in the shared engine, so verified no regression across all engine-based parsers: deepseek, qwen3, gemma4, ling3, minimax, nemotron, seed_oss, etc.). All runs used PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX + -p no:cacheprovider and VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=empty; git status stayed clean.

Verified the new tests are genuine counterfactuals via an in-memory revert (emptying the engine's _tool_end_terminals restores the old fall-through): streaming content regressed to 'plain answer<|end_message|>' / 'plain answer<|content_model_end_sampling|>' while the fixed code yields 'plain answer'. Non-streaming stays correct with only the engine reverted because the abstract_parser.py hunk (returning tool_call_info.content in the no-tool-calls engine path) cleans it there -- so both hunks are load-bearing, one per path, and the two paths agree.

Checked the non-tool-calls branch does not apply the whitespace-only->None normalization used in the tools-called branch; concluded this asymmetry is intentional (with no tools the content is the answer and should not be nulled), not a defect.
